methods.name: bootstrap
methods.desc:
Create the Sprout ASA (full supply to the app) and record admin + pool.
Callable only by the deployer, exactly once. The deployer must fund the app account first so it meets min balance for creating + holding the ASA.
admin / pool_addr are pinned here and can never change (M1, M3). Pass a MULTISIG as `admin` so loss of a single key cannot freeze keyreg/pause.
TESTING: pool_addr is a plain wallet address that receives harvested yield, so the escrow can be exercised without the governance app. Both addresses are validated non-zero and are immutable thereafter. Returns the new ASA id.

methods.name: deposit
methods.desc:
Group: [Payment -> app][this call]. Mints Sprout 1:1 to the depositor.
Returns the amount of Sprout sent (== microAlgo deposited).

methods.name: withdraw
methods.desc:
Group: [AssetTransfer Sprout -> app][this call]. Returns ALGO 1:1.
Withdraw is never pausable and never depends on the governance app. Returns the microAlgo paid out (== Sprout burned-in).

methods.name: harvest
methods.desc:
Sweep (balance - principal - live_mbr - buffer), split 10% admin / 90% pool.
Permissionless: rewards arrive silently as balance increases with no event, so anyone may trigger the sweep. Caller pays the inner-txn fees (now up to TWO inner payments). Returns the TOTAL swept (admin fee + pool), matching the amount by which the account balance drops.
The split is applied to the SURPLUS ONLY. principal, the live MBR, and the C1 buffer all sit below the harvest floor and are never part of `surplus`, so the fee can never come out of depositor principal — I5/I6 hold exactly as before.

methods.name: go_online
methods.desc:
Register the escrow account ONLINE for consensus with the given keys.
Group: [Payment -> escrow (admin-funded)][this call]. The admin attaches a payment that funds the keyreg's fee. When incentive_eligible == 1, the inner keyreg's own fee is set to GO_ONLINE_FEE (2 ALGO) so the protocol sets the IncentiveEligible bit — a prerequisite for earning staking rewards. When 0, a plain online registration (keyreg fee 0) is done.
WHY A GROUPED PAYMENT: the 2 ALGO fee leaves the escrow account's balance. If it came from pooled ALGO it could eat into staker principal — breaking the core invariant. So the ADMIN must supply it: the attached payment, from the admin, tops the escrow up by exactly the fee first. Net effect on the escrow balance is zero, so principal, MBR and buffer are untouched. The payment must come from the admin and cover the fee, or this reverts.
Going online does not change MBR. Participation keys can only vote in consensus, never spend — that is what keeps staking non-custodial.
M2: validate the keys and the round window before registering, so a typo or a stale/expired key set can't put the account online in a broken state (which silently forfeits rewards and can get it marked absent).

methods.name: discard_unbootstrapped
methods.desc:
Delete an app that was CREATED but never bootstrapped (creator-only).
Guards the "created but not bootstrapped → stuck forever" trap: before bootstrap, admin is the zero address, so admin_close's admin check can never pass and the app would otherwise be un-deletable, locking 0.1 ALGO of the creator's min-balance permanently. This lets the original creator tear down such an empty shell.
Strictly limited to the pre-bootstrap state: it asserts sprout_asa_id == 0, so it can NEVER run on a live escrow holding depositor funds. Once bootstrapped, only admin_close (with its principal==0 gate) can delete. No ASA to destroy and the account holds no principal, so it just closes any residual ALGO back to the creator and lets the delete proceed.

methods.name: admin_close
methods.desc:
Destroy the ASA, send all remaining ALGO to admin, and delete the app.
SAFETY GATE: this is permitted ONLY when accounted_principal == 0 — i.e. every unit of Sprout has been burned back and the app holds the FULL supply again, so no depositor has an outstanding claim. While ANY principal is outstanding, this reverts. It can therefore never seize a depositor's funds: the only ALGO it recovers is the residual (MBR + buffer + unharvested surplus), which at principal == 0 is entirely the admin's own.
This preserves the non-custodial guarantee — a compromised admin key still cannot drain staked principal, because it cannot make this call succeed while anyone is staked.
Called as a DeleteApplication so the outer txn tears down the app itself.
